speaker: Doctor
text: Welcome to your appointment. I see you have a history of delayed menarche, unusual physical features, and bone fragility; to understand the underlying cause, can you describe what those specific physical features look like and when your growth spurt ended?

speaker: Patient
text: 16-year-old female. The patient has not experienced menarche. She was noted to have partial labial fusion and clitoromegaly at birth. The patient's mother reports that during pregnancy she had abnormal hair growth on her chin. The patient has a history of severe acne and has sustained fractures following minor trauma. She is currently on oral isotretinoin and an oral contraceptive.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Congenital Adrenal Hyperplasia (CAH) due to 21-hydroxylase deficiency.

The history of ambiguous genitalia at birth, virilization of the mother during pregnancy, and early growth arrest are classic signs of CAH. I need to confirm the hormonal profile to distinguish between salt-wasting and simple virilizing forms. REQUEST TEST: Serum 17-hydroxyprogesterone and electrolytes. REQUEST TEST: 17-OHP level and baseline cortisol/ACTH stimulation test.
